assumptions_and_boundaries.name: IterMut::make_slice
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The target body calls the private macro-expanded helper exactly once. The harness verifies the target call against a narrow external-body helper contract while leaving the helper's raw pointer arithmetic, `len!` macro behavior, and `from_raw_parts` safety preconditions to a separate helper proof/boundary.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: core::ptr::NonNull<T>
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The local Verus tool rejected Rust 1.96 `NonNull<T>` external type specification due trait-bound mismatch in the preceding paired Iter harness. Because target `as_slice` only calls `make_slice`, the field is represented by a target-local opaque stand-in and all pointer/provenance obligations are assigned to the `make_slice` boundary.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: slice_iterator_view::<&IterMut<'a, T>, T>
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The private helper boundary relates its return value to the existing generated shared iterator view; the target body/postcondition is not assumed directly.

notes: Callee closure is narrowed to the single discharged private helper call `make_slice`; no generated target dependency is used.
